fact: 《日英通商航海条约》于1894年7月16日在伦敦签署，自1899年7月17日起生效，宣告以领事裁判权为核心的不平等条约体系终结，1900年的在日外国人已处于条约修订后的新法律环境。

sources.title: Anglo-Japanese Treaty of Commerce and Navigation
sources.quote: The Anglo-Japanese Treaty of Commerce and Navigation (日英通商航海条約, Nichi-Ei Tsūshō Kōkai Jōyaku) signed by Britain and Japan, on 16 July 1894, was a breakthrough agreement; it heralded the end of the unequal treaties and the system of extraterritoriality in Japan. The treaty came into force on 17 July 1899 and lasted until 26 July 1941, less than five months before attack on Pearl Harbor.

fact: 1899年7月17日《日英通商航海条约》生效后，在日英国臣民改受日本法律管辖，英国在日领事法院同日停止管辖（未结案件除外）；条约口岸旧界限制被突破，外国人进入内地不再需要此前的护照许可。

sources.title: Anglo-Japanese Treaty of Commerce and Navigation
sources.quote: When this treaty became effective, British subjects in Japan became subject to Japanese laws instead of British laws. The jurisdiction of the British Supreme Court for China and Japan, the British Court for Japan under it and consular courts in each treaty port ceased on that date, save for pending cases which were allowed to continue.

sources.title: Beyond the Treaty Limits: Pushing the Boundaries in Meiji Japan（Cobbing, Japanese Studies 2025）
sources.quote: As a result, in 1899 the Treaty Limits were no more, and foreigners no longer needed to obtain passports before venturing inland.

fact: 1897年日本颁布《货币法》改行金本位，规定纯金0.75克等于1日元，新币制自1897年10月1日实施；1900年的日本对外贸易与金融结算建立在金本位日元之上。

sources.title: Currency Museum, Bank of Japan — History of Currency
sources.quote: In 1897, Japan enacted the “Currency Act” to introduce the gold standard system, and stipulated that 0.75 g of gold was equivalent to one yen.

sources.title: Lever of Empire: The International Gold Standard and the Crisis of Liberalism in Prewar Japan（Carl Mosk）
sources.quote: In March 1897 the new Coinage Law put the yen on a gold standard as of October 1897, with a value of o-75 grams of gold.

fact: 至1900年前后，三井家族通过金融、矿山、贸易等业务控制数百家企业，以家族血缘而非正式契约联结的财阀形态已经成形；三井物产在生丝、棉纱、煤炭、大米出口中占据主导地位。

sources.title: Reference For Business: Shoei Utsuda 1943—（Mitsui Zaibatsu 条目）
sources.quote: By 1900 the Mitsui family owned hundreds of companies, all united by family rather than formal agreements. This system was known as a zaibatsu.

sources.title: Masuda Takashi（Wikipedia，引述其三井物产经历）
sources.quote: In 1876, at the age of 29, Masuda was appointed the president of Mitsui Trading Company (Mitsui Bussan Kaisha) and contributed to the development of the Mitsui zaibatsu. Mitsui quickly became a dominant player in Japanese exports of silk cloth and thread, cotton, coal, and rice, and in the imports of cotton and other raw materials.

fact: 日本棉纺业纱锭数从1885年的约7万锭增至1900年的108.8万锭，十五年间扩大约14.5倍，机器棉纺织成为明治工业化的主力部门。

fact: 1900年代纺织与织物占日本总出口的49.3%—56.7%；横滨港自1900年起生丝约占该港出口总值的60%；生丝在整个二战前时期始终是日本第一大出口商品。

sources.title: Yokohama | Encyclopedia.com
sources.quote: Yokohama remained the main port for the export of raw silk to the United States. Raw silk accounted for about 60 percent of Yokohama's total export from 1900 onward.
